findings.problem: V1 does not define which legacy seconds remain authoritative during mixed V1/V2 input.
findings.resolution: Final plan makes ticks authoritative when present, validates seconds within half a frame, and keeps seconds as derived compatibility fields.

findings.problem: A file-backed editor could accidentally modify an unrelated absolute JSON path.
findings.resolution: Final plan requires an in-memory editor session bound to a validated Timeline file identity; commands only accept session IDs and allowlisted pointers.

findings.problem: Adding a second mutation implementation inside Command Journal would drift from kacha_delta.
findings.resolution: Extract shared mutation primitives and make delta CLI and Command Journal consume the same implementation.

findings.problem: V1 mentions WGPU but lacks an evidence set and introduces a new toolchain prematurely.
findings.resolution: Rust/WGPU is explicitly deferred. This iteration delivers a provider contract and a fail-closed final-eligibility gate only.

findings.problem: Inspector scope is too broad and could expose fields that require semantic or QC recalculation.
findings.resolution: Final plan restricts the first editable allowlist to timing and safe overlay geometry/opacity; text, media identity, effects, audio routing and release fields remain read-only.

findings.problem: The plan lacks an explicit journal tamper and crash recovery test matrix.
findings.resolution: Final acceptance adds digest-chain validation, truncated-journal recovery, concurrent edit rejection and snapshot restoration tests.

findings.problem: A visual workbench could be misread as a replacement for the Agent-first workflow.
findings.resolution: Final plan defines it as a correction and approval surface; Agent remains the default production entry.
